questions.q: Why is customer feedback important for restaurants?
questions.a: Feedback shows you how guests actually experience your food, service and ambiance, which helps you make better decisions. It points to new menu ideas and things to fix, and asking for it makes guests feel valued. It can also grow your contact list so the relationship continues after the meal.

questions.q: What are the best ways to collect feedback from restaurant guests?
questions.a: Short surveys sent after the visit by text, email or a QR code are one of the easiest ways to gather feedback at volume. Friendly conversations at the table, often around the time guests pay, can bring out more detailed comments. Review sites, social channels and community groups add a broader picture of what people think.

questions.q: How do I get guests to fill out a restaurant feedback survey?
questions.a: Keep the survey short, clear about its purpose and easy to reach, such as a QR code on the receipt or a link right after an order. A small incentive can encourage honest answers. Try not to sound intrusive in the request, because pushy invitations make guests more likely to ignore you.

questions.q: What should I ask about in a restaurant feedback survey?
questions.a: Go beyond an overall score and ask about specific areas: staff and service, the menu, food quality and ambiance. Category-level questions show you exactly which part of the experience needs work. They also give guests an easy way to suggest dishes or changes they'd like to see.

questions.q: How can I manage feedback across several restaurant locations?
questions.a: A feedback management system brings surveys, reviews and other channels into one place so you can act on them quickly. Analytics with sentiment analysis can break feedback down by store, item or category to show where problems repeat. Momos Surveys, for example, collect guest feedback through branded QR codes or links and include these categories out of the box.
